problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav methods either need trained policies or detailed semantic/frontier maps built with detectors. VLM-based agents (e.g. VLMNav) see only a limited egocentric field of view, cannot anticipate outcomes of actions without interacting, and hallucinate.
motivation: Humans imagine room layouts and action outcomes from visual cues before moving. The authors hypothesize that VLMs, trained on vast first-person imagery, hold enough commonsense to act as world models that predict where the goal is likely to be, cutting costly and redundant exploration.
key_idea: Use VLMs as a fully modular world model that predicts goal-presence likelihood per panoramic direction, stores it in an online Curiosity Value Map memory, and feeds subtask/goal-flag feedback and a two-stage action proposer into the policy.
insight: Quantitative, numeric memory (the Curiosity Value Map) is more reliable than free-form text-image memory: text-image memory (SR 62.0) is worse than no memory (67.4), while CVM reaches 70.1 SR with the same subtask decomposition (SD) and no TAP. The two-stage action proposer raises SR from 70.1 to 72.2 but slightly lowers SPL (34.7 to 33.3). Performance scales with VLM strength (Qwen2.5-VL-3B 29.7 SR up to Gemini 1.5 Pro 58.1 on HM3D v0.1).
method: PredictVLM: takes a 6-view panoramic image (rotations 30°–330°) and scores 0-10 the likelihood of the goal being in each direction
Curiosity Value Map: top-down map initialised to 10; navigable-area scores are projected via depth and pose and fused with the previous map by pixel-wise min; explored goal-free areas go to 0
Direction selection: map values are projected back to the panorama and averaged per direction; the highest-scoring direction's image is chosen

Subtask decomposition with cost: PlanVLM takes the selected image and the previous subtask and outputs a new subtask and a goal flag; these serve as cost/feedback that configures the PlanVLM and ReasonVLM prompts, with no fine-tuning

Action proposer (exploration stage): samples K polar-coordinate actions in the navigable area, filters explored regions, limits distance and angle, annotates them on the image, and ReasonVLM (ActionVLM) picks one

Goal-approaching stage: once the goal is flagged, distance limits are removed and sampling is denser; GoalVLM picks the vector pointing to the goal location, and the agent stops when the Euclidean distance is below d_thres instead of using a VLM stop decision

setting.backbone: Gemini 1.5 Pro (frozen) for the main results; also Gemini 1.5/2.0 Flash and Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D 640x480, HFoV 79°, pitch 14°, six views combined into a panorama, plus pose
setting.action_space: polar-coordinate (r, θ) waypoint-like actions chosen from annotated candidates; max 40 navigation steps
setting.privileged: none (depth and pose used, as standard in ObjectNav)

results: WMNav beats all zero-shot baselines: on HM3D 58.1 SR / 31.2 SPL (+3.2 SR and +3.2 SPL over the best baselines) and on MP3D 45.4 SR / 17.2 SPL (+13.5 SR over SGM's 37.7 and +1.1 SPL). It also has the best SPL on HM3D and the best SR on MP3D among all methods, including supervised ones.
limitations: Depends heavily on strong proprietary VLMs; open-source Qwen2.5-VL-7B gets only 46.1 SR and 3B only 29.7 SR on HM3D
Requires many VLM calls per step (predict, plan, reason), with panoramic capture costing extra steps; no real-robot validation
The two-stage proposer lowers SPL slightly in the ablation (34.7 to 33.3), and the ablations do not isolate each component's variance
